audit.kind: read-only Knip and pnpm ast integration audit
audit.head: ec84ed686

rosterControl.claim: Knip package workspace keys equal native packages/* workspace membership.

posture.issueRules: all configured issue classes error except cycles warn

focusedControl.claim: Default Knip includes tooling dependencies; production excludes tooling while retaining application dependency reporting.

astRelationship.negativeSearchResult: Only prose mentions of Knip remain; no Knip config import or output reader exists.

worldSelection.claim: The semantic workspace reads native compiler programs and prefers the world-predicted primary owner when present.

astRelationship.sharedOrSeparate: Knip remains a separate workspace graph. It shares package membership through a parity test but does not consume native world intent, compiler-program descriptors, or generated TS config intent.

lensDetails.relationship: Uses semantic references across native programs and partitions package, tooling, and test sites.
Uses resolved declaration identity and separate production/test liveness sets.
Independently classifies cross-package, same-package, tooling, and test consumers, including type-only public imports.
Derives runtime entries from package exports, package scripts, package-root tool configs, and client main.tsx; it no longer reads Knip analysis roots.

trackedRepairs.status: The candidate-lens repair moved typed AST analysis onto native worlds and removed prodonly's dependency on Knip analysis roots; the implementation was independently confirmed.
Graph/query lens repair is committed and independently confirmed; it is separate from Knip configuration integration.

conservativeTradeoffs.area: wildcard package exports and index barrels
conservativeTradeoffs.risk: Published or explicitly configured index entries are treated as live, and entry exports are outside ordinary unused-export reporting even when no runtime consumer imports them.
All scripts and broad tooling front doors are entries, so their unused exports can be false-live to Knip. Runtime-discovered gates and shell-spawned tools would otherwise be false-dead.
Default Knip lets tests keep application exports alive; full-tier knip:prod supplies the test-only delta, while AST testonly directly classifies it.

The client type-imports AppRouter from the server entry barrel. Knip can treat the entry export as public regardless of runtime use; AST apisurface can identify it as PUBLIC and type-only. The router value remains runtime-live through the server app entry.
A runtime schema referenced only by z.infer can look alive to import/export reachability while being runtime-dead. AST typeonly-alive retains this as a real candidate.

Published schema barrels and star re-exports keep table exports conservatively live; Knip cannot adjudicate dead columns, whole-row reflection, or individual table members. AST columns and the orphan ratchet own those questions.
Default-content assets and showcase plugin bundles are intentionally outside Knip project globs, so Knip cannot prove their byte-level liveness.

conservativeTradeoffs.classification: latent maintenance risk, not a confirmed current defect
conservativeTradeoffs.risk: A future computed loader, shell-spawned entry, or shipped-byte surface can be false-dead until its runtime authority is modeled in entries or a reasoned ignore.

confirmedDefects.classification: confirmed source contradiction in existing issue 2535 scope
confirmedDefects.summary: Issue #2535 removed prodonly's import of knip.ts, but the reviewed grant, policy rationale, and real-tree family assertion still require that import.
confirmedDefects.impact: The real-tree family test will fail, and a complete entire-population policy run should report the reviewed grant as stale through zero consumption.
confirmedDefects.suggestedWork: Fold into #2535: delete the stale reviewed-grant row and retire or update its Knip-specific real-tree assertions and comments. Do not open a separate work item.

conclusion: No separate Knip/AST integration defect was confirmed beyond the stale #2535 grant residue. The remaining mismatches are explicit conservative tradeoffs or analysis-boundary choices.
